evidence.quote: We present a rare case

patients.label: 17-year-old right-hand-dominant male football player with left middle finger FDS avulsion and PIP fracture-dislocation

summary.text: A 17-year-old right-hand-dominant male presented with acute pain, swelling and deformity of the left middle finger after an injury 3 days earlier in a football game, with a sudden tearing sensation. Examination showed swelling, effusion, tenderness, limited painful motion and instability at the PIP joint, with normal sensation and brisk capillary refill.

Three-view radiographs of the left hand showed a comminuted articular fracture of the base of the middle phalanx and dorsal subluxation of the PIP joint, consistent with a dorsal fracture-dislocation. The abstract describes FDS avulsion with an intact FDP.

Urgent surgical repair under sedation and local anesthesia included a Brunner incision, PIP joint exposure, disimpaction and reduction of fragments, K-wire fixation replaced with screws, and anchor repair of the FDS tendon. The FDS tendon was absent from the field with only the FDP present. Fluoroscopy confirmed alignment and fixation, and the incision was closed with a dressing and dorsal blocking splint.

Postoperatively pain was well controlled, the incision healed, sutures were removed and composite flexion was within 1 cm of the palm. At a follow-up visit he had resumed basketball and weightlifting without pain, had a slight PIP flexion contracture, and six-week postoperative imaging showed union; he was cleared to return to all sports. He completed 20 hand therapy sessions with range-of-motion measurements at the first and last sessions, and the abstract reports full functional recovery.
